h1: Compact hydraulic press brakes — 16 to 66 US tons, 2 to 8 ft
intro: A compact hydraulic press brake bends sheet between a punch and a V-die like its big brothers, at the size that fits a sheet-metal shop rather than a steel-fabrication plant: 2 to 8 ft of bending length and 16 to 66 US tons, on a footprint that goes through a door and runs on a 600 V or 208 V supply. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, both on this page: the ISITAN Edgebender, made in Turkey — the 1240 CNC with independent Y1 / Y2 cylinders and a Cybelec touchscreen, and the 1230, 1540 and 2160 NC with a motorized back gauge, 33 to 66 tons over 4.2 to 6.9 ft, Promecam tooling and a Leuze light guard; and NovoTech's own value-line HBV bending brakes, 16 to 35 tons, with a four-way V-block (HBV24 / 48) or two cylinders (HBV-1250 / 2540) for brackets, clips and short parts in plate to 3/16″. For HVAC fittings, enclosures, signage, brackets and job-shop work where a 100-ton machine is more than you need. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel and a 1-year warranty, installed, trained and supported from Mississauga, ON, Canada. For 10 ft and longer, or 1/4″ plate and up, see the hydraulic press brakes; for a brake with no hydraulic oil the electric press brakes.

faq.a: Bending force depends on the sheet thickness, the bend length and the V-die opening: in mild steel about 575 × t² ÷ V US tons per foot, with t and V in inches. In a V of 8 × the thickness, a 4 ft bend takes about 16 US tons in 16 ga, 39 tons in 10 ga and 47 tons in 8 ga (0.16″); a wider die lowers the force — 8 ga in a 2″ V takes about 31 tons over 4 ft — at the cost of a larger inside radius. The control calculates the exact force for the tool and material you enter; send us your thickest and longest bend and we size the machine.

The 2-axis NC Edgebender sets the bending angle (Y) and the back gauge (X) from a program — enough for most job-shop bending. The 3-axis CNC Edgebender 1240 controls the two cylinders independently (Y1, Y2), so the beam can be tilted for compensation, and the Cybelec Cybtouch 12 gives graphic programming, angle correction and tool libraries like a full-size CNC press brake.

The Edgebender is a press brake: a programmable ram, a motorized back gauge, Promecam tooling and a light guard, for 4 – 7 ft sheet work all day. The HBV is a hydraulic bending brake for short parts in plate — brackets, clips, tabs — bent on a four-way V-block (HBV24 / 48) or between two cylinders (HBV-1250 / 2540) with a hand-wheel back gauge, at a fraction of the price. If you bend panels and enclosures, the Edgebender; if you bend 3/16″ plate brackets a few at a time, the HBV.

The Edgebenders use Promecam-style (European) quick-release clamping, the most common tooling standard in Canada, with a standard top tool and bottom die included. Segmented punches, gooseneck tools and special dies are available from NovoTech's Eurostamp press brake tooling stock. The HBV brakes come with their V-block or V-die.

faq.q: Are they safe to run without a separate guarding system?
faq.a: Every Edgebender carries a Leuze front light guard with learning mode, side covers with safety switches, a programmable back gauge retract and a CE-compliant foot pedal with emergency stop; DSP and Fiessler laser systems are available as options. In Ontario a new press brake needs a pre-start health and safety review (PSR) under Regulation 851 before it runs; NovoTech prepares the documentation for it.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — every press brake is shipped to Mississauga, ON, Canada, unloaded, levelled, commissioned and the operators trained by NovoTech; Dener Canada and NovoTech stock the parts here. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request), a 1-year warranty and remote diagnostics through the control.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
